title: YouTube as a Source of Medical and Epidemiological Information During COVID-19 Pandemic: A Cross-Sectional Study of Content Across Six Languages Around the Globe
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 240 YouTube videos (40 per language x 6 languages) retrieved by COVID-19 keywords on 8 April 2020. Videos were coded into four non-overlapping content categories against CDC/WHO material by two independent language-proficient reviewers, and 24/240 (10%) were classified as Misleading. This is a quantitative share of items in a sample judged inaccurate against an external ground truth, with a stated denominator -> CONTENT. DISCERN and MICI indices are additionally reported and are coded as QUALITY.

estimates.country: Six languages around the globe (English, Arabic, Bengali, Dutch, Hindi, Nigerian Pidgin); author teams in India, Egypt, Netherlands, Nigeria
estimates.measure_type: % of sampled YouTube COVID-19 videos classified as medically misleading
estimates.denominator: 240 YouTube videos (the first 40 videos meeting inclusion criteria out of the top 120 search results, in each of six languages) returned by two COVID-19 keywords per language
estimates.definition: A video was counted in the numerator if coded into the non-overlapping category 'Misleading': content that is scientifically inaccurate or makes ambiguous claims that are not evidence-based, judged against CDC and WHO publications/guidelines
estimates.misinfo_def: "Misleading-content that is scientifically inaccurate or makes ambiguous claims that are not evidence-based"
estimates.source_quote: Altogether, 139 (52.5%) videos were classified as informative, 57 (23.75%) as news updates, and 20 (8.33%) as personal experiences. Twenty-four videos (10%) were flagged as misleading
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 4; Table 3; also Abstract ('Ten percent of videos were found to present medically misleading information.')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Each video independently reviewed by two authors/volunteers of a medical background proficient in the video's language; CDC and WHO website content taken as the scientific standard; inter-observer agreement kappa = 0.88 overall (0.70 Dutch to 1.00 English), all P < .01
estimates.moderator_quote: For this study, the content of websites of the CDC and the WHO was considered as standard and scientifically up-to-date.
estimates.notes: Denominator is a rank-truncated, keyword-driven set (top 120 screened, first 40 eligible kept per language) -> denom_scope topical + denom_selection curated. Videos non-medical in content (political, economic) were excluded before the 40 were fixed, so the denominator is COVID-19 medical/epidemiological video content, not all COVID-19 video content. Country coded Global: the sample is defined by language, not by nation, and no per-country figures are reported.

estimates.country: Six languages around the globe (English, Arabic, Bengali, Dutch, Hindi, Nigerian Pidgin)
estimates.measure_type: Mean modified DISCERN content-reliability score of sampled COVID-19 videos (scale 0-5)
estimates.denominator: 240 YouTube videos (40 per language, six languages) returned by two COVID-19 keywords per language
estimates.definition: Five-item modified DISCERN instrument (aims clear; reliable sources used; balanced/unbiased; additional sources listed; areas of uncertainty mentioned), 1 point per affirmative answer, 0-5 total
estimates.misinfo_def: "Misleading-content that is scientifically inaccurate or makes ambiguous claims that are not evidence-based"
estimates.source_quote: The overall mean DISCERN score was 2.62 ± 1.32.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent language-proficient medical reviewers per language applying a five-item modified DISCERN tool adapted from Bora et al., Khatri et al. and Singh et al.; overall kappa 0.88
estimates.moderator_quote: The reliability of the information provided by the videos was graded on a scale adapted from the modified DISCERN tool used in previous studies on similar subjects
estimates.notes: QUALITY row, kept for the appendix only and excluded from prevalence per INSTRUCTIONS section 3 (DISCERN scores -> QUALITY). A wholly accurate video can score low on DISCERN (e.g. by not listing additional sources), so this is not a falsity share. The parallel MICI index (mean total 5.68 +/- 4.22 out of 25) is the same kind of measure and is not given a separate row.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Table 3 gives the misleading share separately for each of the six LANGUAGES: English 2 (5%), Arabic 5 (12.5%), Bengali 3 (7.5%), Dutch 1 (2.5%), Hindi 6 (15%), Nigerian Pidgin 7 (17.5%), each out of 40 videos. These are language strata, not countries or platforms, so per the one-row-per-country-x-platform-x-measure rule I kept only the pooled 24/240 = 10%. An adjudicator wanting language-level rows would find them fully verbatim in Table 3. (2) Table 3 also reports the misleading category's share of VIEWS within each language sample (English 3.99%, Arabic 0.43%, Bengali 8.10%, Dutch 0.63%, Hindi 41.50%, Nigerian Pidgin 7.30%). By the denominator rule a share of views is EXPOSURE, but the denominator is only the views accrued by that language's 40 sampled videos, not any population's viewing diet, so I judged these too artefactual to enter as exposure estimates; no pooled view share is stated and computing one would be a cross-category sum barred by R8. (3) 'Eighteen (75%) of these were from independent users' is the source composition INSIDE the 24 misleading videos, not a falsity share, so no row (it is not the R3 case either). (4) DISCERN threshold shares (22 videos, 9.16%, scored 0; 33 videos, 13.75%, scored 5) and MICI coverage shares (e.g. 177 (73.75%) videos made no mention of screening/diagnosis) are quality/coverage shares, not falsity shares; not extracted. (5) The 25 verbatim misleading statements in Appendix Table 10 are an all-false list with no denominator.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Sampling frame: YouTube search on 8 April 2020 with the two highest-yield COVID-19 keywords in each of six languages, browser cache cleared and a new account used; top 120 results screened per language and the first 40 meeting inclusion/exclusion criteria retained (n = 240). Non-medical (political/economic) and duplicate videos excluded. Coding procedure: each video independently rated by two authors/volunteers of medical background proficient in that language; four non-overlapping content categories plus modified DISCERN (0-5) and MICI (0-25) indices; CDC and WHO publications used as the reference standard. Reliability: kappa = 0.88 overall, by language 0.85 Arabic, 0.76 Bengali, 0.70 Dutch, 1.00 English, 0.82 Hindi, 0.88 Nigerian Pidgin, all P < .01. No response-rate concept (item-level design). Limitations acknowledged: only two keywords per language, cross-sectional snapshot, videos already removed by YouTube could not be captured.
